sections.content: Use *mientras* to connect two actions that happened at the same time. It shows that one action was happening while another was happening. In this unit, practise the connector with past actions and keep the focus on describing what happened during the same period.

items.spanish: Mientras trabajamos, hablamos con los voluntarios.
items.english: While we worked, we spoke with the volunteers.

items.spanish: Mientras limpiamos el parque, plantamos flores.
items.english: While we cleaned the park, we planted flowers.

items.spanish: Mientras recogimos basura, otros voluntarios limpiaron el lago.
items.english: While we collected rubbish, other volunteers cleaned the lake.

items.spanish: Mientras comimos, hablamos con los voluntarios.
items.english: While we ate, we spoke with the volunteers.

sections.content: Further along you'll meet *mientras* with the *imperfecto* for a background action, like *mientras cocinaba*. Watch out: with -ar verbs the *nosotros* form is the same in the present and the preterite (*trabajamos*), as you saw in Unit 11, so the English and the other verb in the sentence show the tense. For now, with the *pretérito* *indefinido* on both sides, *mientras* just glues two completed events into the same stretch of time.
